- Key constraints: HIPAA-adjacent data flows for a subset of users, single-tenant requirement for pilot, 12-week procurement window.

Hi Alex — following up on the items from the call, attaching the benchmark PDF with measured numbers from a Dedicated instance (A100 equivalent, q4 quantized model) using a representative prompt profile you described. Key highlights from our runs:

- p50 / p95 / p99 (single-token first-token latency, avg over 1h): 14ms / 98ms / 210ms for seq len 64, batching at target concurrency of 2k.
- Sustained throughput: ~1,200 requests/sec with 4k token windows when leveraging KV cache and continuous batching (p95 targets maintained with the configured autoscale).
- Cold-start median: ~700ms (we recommend a warm pool for SLA-sensitive endpoints).
- Multi-region failover: replication adds ~15-25ms typical regional penalty; we can keep primary in us-west and failover to us-east in seconds via smart routing.

Notes on configuration and tradeoffs are in the attached PDF. Short answers to your questions: we support per-route quantization profiles, prefix caching, and can pin model versions for the pilot. If you need exact load shapes run against your prompt set, send a small anonymized sample and we’ll run the same harness.

Attachments: latency-benchmarks-20260223.pdf, redwood-sla-summary.pdf

Let me know if anything needs more detail — happy to jump on a 30-min deep technical sync with your infra team.

— Dev
